title: AI Daily Briefing
description: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, open and local models, and AI in defense.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 5–13. New: Google said Nov. 12 that Gemini 4 Hydrogen is available for agentic work, OpenAI described the same day how automated red teaming improved jailbreak resistance in GPT-6 Astra, and Air & Space Forces Magazine reported the Department of the Air Force is applying an AI strategy across 15 mission areas. The Nov. 5 Moonshot export note, the Nov. 5 Gemini Omni item, and the Nov. 6 Hacktron partnership note were dropped to stay inside the count. No new Anthropic product post dated Nov. 12–13 was opened. Tom's Hardware's Nov. 12 writeup of TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max tracks a Nov. 9 Google post and was not added as a new announcement. The Open and Local Models subsection is empty. Nvidia's resignation is on the partners page.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and restricts Mythos 5.2 to vetted cyber and biology work
items.summary: Anthropic said Nov. 9 that Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are the same underlying model, with improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision. Anthropic said Fable has cybersecurity and biology safeguards so it can be offered to all users, while organizations doing cybersecurity or biomedical research can apply for Mythos through the Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs. Anthropic said the models generate output up to 30 percent faster than Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, with an optional fast mode up to 2.5 times quicker at $16 and $80. Anthropic said Fable 5.2 is available on Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, and that Claude Enterprise customers can use Claude Security with Mythos 5.2.

items.headline: OpenAI says automated red teaming made GPT-6 Astra refuse more cyber jailbreaks
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 12 that it used automated red teaming to improve what it calls fuzzy robustness, how reliably a model withholds disallowed help under jailbreak pressure in dual-use areas such as cyber and biology. OpenAI said the method was used to train GPT-6 Astra and Sol, and that on a fixed set of earlier cyber jailbreaks GPT-6 Astra answered 91.5 percent safely, compared with 59 percent for GPT-5.6 Sol. OpenAI said those measurements are of the model without production safeguards, and that deployed high-stakes cyber and biology use still goes through the Daybreak and Rosalind trusted-access programs. OpenAI said the robustness-trained GPT-6 Astra was not more likely to refuse benign tasks.

items.headline: OpenAI opens Businesses in ChatGPT, with U.S. agents for eligible sellers
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 10 that Businesses in ChatGPT is in beta, so a business can claim a profile in Business Hub, update details, add product feeds with pricing and availability, and see aggregated mentions and website clicks. OpenAI said it does not share users' conversations or Business Agent chats with businesses. OpenAI said eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the United States can launch a Business Agent that customers start from the business profile, in a conversation labeled as separate from their ChatGPT chat. OpenAI said businesses can sponsor that agent as a destination for ChatGPT ads, and that ChatGPT has 1.2 billion weekly users.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen for faster agentic work, priced below Carbon
items.summary: Google said Nov. 12 that Gemini 4 Hydrogen is available for coding and agentic work in Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, and Google Search. Google said the price is flat across a 1 million-token context window, at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, and that at the default high thinking level Hydrogen scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, compared with 50 for Gemini 4 Argon. Google said Orchestrator in Google Antigravity can switch between Carbon and Hydrogen in one session and, on Terminal-Bench 4.0, reached near-Carbon task success while using 24 percent less quota and finishing 19 percent faster. Google said free users of the Gemini app get Hydrogen through automatic model selection when it fits the prompt.

items.headline: Google opens the Gemini Decisions API, scoring up to 1,000 questions in one pass
items.summary: Google said Nov. 11 that the Gemini Decisions API is available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, powered by a new Gemini Decision 1 model. Google said a request can pair one multimodal input of up to 256,000 tokens, including text, images, audio, video, and PDFs, with up to 1,000 yes/no, multiple-choice, or rubric questions, and that the model returns probabilities and confidence scores in 150 to 250 milliseconds. Google said the price is $0.10 per million input tokens with no output tokens billed, and that on a shared benchmark suite it is nearly five times cheaper than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite used through the Interactions API. Google said support in Gemini on Google Cloud is coming soon.

items.headline: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon generally available and opens a cybersecurity track
items.summary: Google said Nov. 10 that Gemini 4 Carbon is available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers, and that it is the company's strongest model for cybersecurity and long-horizon agentic work. Google said Carbon is priced the same as Gemini 4 Argon during an introductory period, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, and that the price becomes $4 and $20 after Nov. 30, 2026. Google said Carbon for cyber, available through the Fairwind Program, leads its benchmarks for finding, exploiting, and patching vulnerabilities, and that Google's Cloud Vulnerability Research team used it to show two bugs in a popular open-source project were exploitable at a severity Google compared to PHP2Shell. Google said Wiz, in its Scan for Good program, used Carbon to find zero-days at two major SaaS providers in under two hours.

items.headline: WIRED: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally verified parts of the Signal protocol
items.summary: WIRED reported Nov. 10 that Google DeepMind researchers used a framework called AlphaProof Code to formally verify a number of the Signal protocol's cryptographic guarantees in a four-week proof of concept. WIRED said the analysis did not find new vulnerabilities in the portions it examined, and that on older Signal versions with known, long-fixed flaws the tool identified the bugs and showed those versions could not be formally verified. WIRED said the work did not cover the entire Signal mobile app, and that the researchers are releasing the specification and proof. Signal chief technology officer Ehren Kret said the approach expands on earlier formal verification that covered smaller portions of the code.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: two firms cleared to buy Nvidia H200 chips had empty offices
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 8, citing The New York Times, that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and that receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them. Tom's Hardware said the companies' executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for providing advanced technology to the Chinese military, and it named the two firms New Matrix and Maginfra. It said better-known approved buyers include Baidu, BYD, Tesla Shanghai, ZTE, Alibaba, Tencent, and ByteDance. Former White House National Security Council China director Liza Tobin told the Times she has concerns that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed to ensure licensing terms are followed.

items.headline: Federal News Network: Justice Department sets up a Super Intelligence Task Force
items.summary: Federal News Network's Nov. 6 newscast said the Justice Department's new Super Intelligence Task Force will coordinate the use and oversight of artificial intelligence across the agency. The outlet said a memo issued Thursday outlined six focus areas. It said initial duties include organizing the department's criminal and civil law enforcement efforts involving AI, and deconflicting investigations, cases, and other matters among components and U.S. attorneys' offices by applying AI tools. The department will merge its Artificial Intelligence Task Force, created in January, into the new one.

items.headline: Air Force applies an AI strategy across 15 mission areas, including nuclear operations
items.summary: Air & Space Forces Magazine reported Nov. 12 that the Department of the Air Force is applying an artificial intelligence strategy across 15 mission areas, from intelligence and human resources to nuclear operations. Chief Data and AI Officer Susan Davenport described the plan at the GovCIO AI Summit on Nov. 6 in Tysons, Virginia, and said each area will be overseen by a general officer or senior civilian who tracks governance and data access. She said the data strategy leaves data with the organizations that produce it, instead of copying it through a central team that tags and cleans it. The department told the magazine the blueprint is controlled unclassified information and was not released, and that domain principals will present roadmaps at a showcase in early 2027.

items.headline: Helsing unveils Clarity, a European platform that keeps a person on the trigger
items.summary: Helsing said Nov. 11 in Berlin that it unveiled Clarity, an agentic intelligence platform developed and built in Europe that processes sensor feeds, open sources, written reports, and systems a unit already runs. Helsing said the platform uses hundreds of military-specific agents to detect adversary assets and prepare the information a weapon needs, and that it follows MOSA principles and relevant NATO standards and runs on infrastructure the customer owns. Helsing said an operator reviews the evidence, selects each asset, and authorizes every hand-off to a weapon, and that a target is nominated only when independent sources agree. Co-CEO Gundbert Scherf said European armed forces get software that stays under their control.

items.headline: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber for approved Daybreak Red customers
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 5 that GPT-6 Cyber finds and validates vulnerabilities inside a researcher-set scope, and that it is available first through the API and Codex to a select group of approved Daybreak Red customers. OpenAI said it scores 48.5 percent on ExploitGym, up from 32.1 percent for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and that without a deployment prompt it avoided exploiting out-of-scope services in 99.93 percent of ExploitGym Honeypot tests. OpenAI said its researchers used the model to develop 948 privilege-escalation exploits in Linux and to identify 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities, and that Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, and CrowdStrike described using it. OpenAI said it classifies the model as Critical under its Preparedness Framework, up from High for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and it quoted Dragos chief AI officer Rob Lee, after lab evaluations of Daybreak Red models, saying a frontier model on a mock power-plant range found two zero-days in software that manages protective-relay data.
